paper.title: Architecting Scalable Trapped Ion Quantum Computers using Surface Codes

artifact.note: The README says MIT but the repository has no license file: we ran it locally and publish only the schedules it produced.

paper.what: A compiler for surface-code rounds on grid, linear and switch QCCD devices, and a design-space study of trap capacity, wiring and logical error.

runs.label: rotated surface code d=2, one round, grid, capacity 2

checks.broadcast: skipped: transport is not broadcast in this model

results.title: Every operation finds its ions where it says they are
A site holds at most its capacity
A junction holds one ion at a time
A rail carries at most its capacity
A two-ion gate acts on two ions standing in one site
An ion does one thing at a time
A split takes the ion at the end of its chain, or pays to reorder
Every two-qubit gate of the circuit is performed, and no other
Each qubit's gates keep the circuit's order, up to commuting CNOTs
examples: c1 = circuit operation 5 (cx 6,7), c2 = circuit operation 6 (cx 12,6): end(last(c1)) is t = 2370 µs and start(first(c2)) is t = 1530 µs

results.title: One operation at a time in a trap
Every operation lasts what the clock says
Operations that hold the same component never overlap

first_violations.message: 1 qubit(s) see their gates in an order the circuit does not allow (e.g. ['34'])

ours_boxes.title: Ours, WISE control
ours_boxes.how: Broadcast control on Jones's junction grid: the same geometry, mapping and native operations, exact per-qubit Stim order, one geometric transport class per cycle. Every idle trap declares a per-site switch; intra/inter transport and gates do not overlap.
ours_boxes.found: All four split schedules retain full searched distance in both memory bases. Last start is 4070 µs (makespan 4120 µs); John's current Ours is faster. No waveform switching cost is charged. This is broadcast control on Jones's junction grid.
